beginner.headline: Today (Fri Oct 16): conditional for beginners. Best 6:45–9:30 AM around the 8:13 AM high (1.8 ft), before the NE trades and gusts build and before the long-period south swell peaks later today. Canoes reported 1–3 ft faces (SNN) to 2–3 ft thigh–waist (Surfline, untimed). Late morning conditional; from 11:30 AM not recommended.
beginner.recommendation: Go early: 6:45–9:30 AM has the most water over the reef (8:13 AM high, 1.8 ft) and the lightest wind of the day. NWS has NE 15–20 mph today and the model has gusts in the mid-to-high 20s mph by mid-morning; at Waikīkī that is cross-offshore, so expect seaward drift that grows through the morning. The 17–19 s south swell is up and holding and forecast to peak later today (HNN, Surfline forecaster), with NWS holding south-facing shores at 4–6 ft all day: at Canoes that means long lulls and occasional bigger sets, not low energy. Watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before starting. Check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low and sets aren't reaching the inside. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.headline: No DOH brown-water advisory for Waikīkī; bacteria and sewage lists not read, so water quality at Canoes is not verified
water.statement: The DOH brown-water advisory list was read this morning: no Waikīkī entry, and no open Oʻahu brown-water advisory (Bellows–Sherwood closed Oct 15; the only open one statewide is ʻAnini Beach, Kauaʻi). The bacteria and sewage-spill lists were not read, so nothing can be said about those for Waikīkī or Oʻahu. A bacteria advisory at Waimea Bay (Oʻahu North Shore) is reported still in effect by a third-party repost; it is not a Waikīkī notice. Not finding an advisory does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: The eha-cloud brown-water event list loaded (all rows read); the full advisory list covering bacteria and sewage did not. Mostly sunny Friday morning lowers runoff risk at Waikīkī but proves nothing; showers increase this afternoon and tonight.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
